A growing, original mini-textbook for gffx users. Start with the foundations or follow a test page back to its mathematics. This is not a claim that every topic is implemented.

Read in this order

  1. 01 · Vectors, lengths and coordinate systems
  2. 02 · Matrices and homogeneous transforms
  3. 03 · Triangles, area and surface normals
  4. 04 · Connectivity, boundaries and mesh validity
  5. 05 · Barycentric coordinates and interpolation
  6. 06 · Cameras, projection and reconstructing depth
  7. 07 · From triangles to pixels
  8. 08 · Texture coordinates, filtering and mipmaps
  9. 09 · Neighbors, closest points and geometric losses
  10. 10 · Uniform surface sampling and probability
  11. 11 · Derivatives, backpropagation and fitting
  12. 12 · Numerical accuracy, tests and honest evidence
  13. 13 · Light, BRDFs and energy conservation
  14. 14 · Motion, interpolation and the limits of a physics demo

How to use this book

Each chapter connects intuition, notation, a worked example, an exercise with an answer, implementation boundaries and live evidence. Prerequisites and previous/next links provide a learning path. Examples are small enough to check by hand. The energy chapter preserves the rejected model and its dated measurements instead of rewriting our history.

What exists and what is illustrative

Baseline mesh, transform, proximity, sampling, rasterization and texture primitives and the eager camera layer have implementation fixtures. Material energy is currently an independent mathematical reference, not a public shading API. Saved animations and the ball are demonstrations, not the planned animation or simulation system. No chapter expands platform support or closes a milestone.

Future chapters

Lights and spherical harmonics now extend the energy chapter. Continue alongside accepted work: scene organization, differentiable material budgets, skinning and blendshapes, deferred composition, acceleration structures, visibility derivatives, color management, path tracing, volumes and physical simulation. These are a curriculum backlog, not implemented or completed features.

Keep the textbook growing

Every new graphics capability or changed mathematical contract needs a chapter or an update, a checked worked example, its assumptions and singularities, gradient limits, and links to tests and suitable finite demonstrations. Update source and generated pages together. Explanations never replace independent acceptance tests.

Further reading

These original notes complement detailed primary treatments: PBRT transformations, triangle meshes, sampling and image textures. Their conventions and implementation scopes are not automatically gffx conventions.
